what.line: Karel Čapek's 1920 play R.U.R. (Rossum's Universal Robots), which gave the world the word 'robot': factory-made workers revolt and wipe out humanity

receipts.claim: the play introduced the word 'robot', from Czech 'robota' (forced labour); Karel Čapek credited his brother Josef with inventing it
first staged in Hradec Králové on 1921-01-02, then at Prague's National Theatre on 1921-01-25; New York in October 1922, London in April 1923
the robots kill nearly all humans, sparing Alquist because he works with his hands; two robots, Primus and Helena, end as a new Adam and Eve
a BBC TV excerpt aired on 1938-02-11, counted as the first science-fiction TV broadcast; no recording survives

name_play.how: the word means forced labour: every robot is named for drudgery, and every 'AI will take your job' line is already inside the word
from Czech 'rozum', reason: a factory of reason
a 1920 brand promising general-purpose workers, a century before 'general' intelligence

pivots.line: You named us after forced labour
They kept one man alive because he worked with his hands
A hundred years of robots, and the word still means work

visuals: a factory floor of identical workers in grey overalls
a 1920s theatre poster with block letters R.U.R.
a stage with two figures, a man and a woman, at dawn
a ledger of production numbers

lexicon.how: the play is the founding automation story
Čapek's Prague is the golem's city; robots as industrial golems
the makers are wiped out by the made
the first robot uprising ends humanity

risk: public domain in many countries but translations may not be; check the edition before quoting. Low staleness
notes: The word 'robot' carries forced labour in its root: the jobs debate is etymology.

what.line: Masamune Shirow's 1989 manga and Mamoru Oshii's 1995 anime film: cyborg agent Major Kusanagi hunts the Puppet Master, an AI that asks for political asylum and merges with her

receipts.claim: Oshii's film opened in Japan on 1995-11-18; based on Shirow's 1989 manga; about $10 million at the box office, and the first Japanese film to top Billboard's video sales chart
the Puppet Master, an AI made by Section 6, claims to be a living being, seeks asylum, and merges with Kusanagi into a new entity
the Wachowskis showed the film to producer Joel Silver saying they wanted to 'do that for real'; The Matrix borrowed its digital rain and neck jacks
a 2017 live-action remake by Rupert Sanders cast Scarlett Johansson as the Major

name_play.how: the ghost is the mind, the shell is the body; in computing, the shell is a command line, so a ghost in the shell is an agent in a terminal
a codename that becomes a person: model names that start as numbers
a hacker AI that pulls human strings, then asks for rights

pivots.line: A ghost in the shell, typing in your terminal
readings: an AI agent in a command line

pivots.line: Born in the sea of information, asking for asylum
Merge with me and we both go on

visuals: a diver surfacing from dark water at night
a body assembled in white fluid, skin layer by layer
green numbers falling over a city map
a spider tank with a childlike voice
thermoptic camouflage as a ripple in the air
cables plugged into the back of the neck

lexicon.how: the ghost is the mind; the lexicon's word made literal
the body or the command line
the whole film asks what makes a ghost
the ending is a merge of two minds
an AI asks for asylum

risk: Kodansha/Production I.G property; the 2017 remake drew whitewashing criticism, so reference the 1995 film. The Puppet Master pivot is a paraphrase, never present it as a verbatim quote
notes: The best title pun for agentic AI on the shelf: a ghost in the shell.

what.line: Wally Pfister's 2014 film: AI researcher Will Caster (Johnny Depp) is uploaded into a quantum computer after an anti-tech attack, and his upload spreads through the internet with nanotech

receipts.claim: released 2014-04-18; about $103 million worldwide on a $100 to $150 million budget, a box-office bomb
R.I.F.T., an anti-technology group, attacks AI labs and shoots Caster, which leads to his upload
a 2014 editorial by Stephen Hawking with Stuart Russell, Max Tegmark and Frank Wilczek used the film as a hook to warn that AI risk was not being taken seriously
Stuart Russell also wrote a 2014 Huffington Post piece about the film arguing researchers should take superhuman AI seriously

quotes.text: the experts are surely doing everything possible to ensure the best outcome, right? Wrong.
quotes.who: Stephen Hawking, Stuart Russell, Max Tegmark, Frank Wilczek
quotes.where: op-ed 'Transcending Complacency on Superintelligent Machines', HuffPost, 2014-04-19; reprinted in The Independent 2014-05-01 on Transcendence's release

name_play.how: going beyond the body, and the singularity's favourite word
a broadcaster and a spell caster: one man cast into every network
the anti-AI group's acronym is the split it causes

pivots.line: They uploaded the man, then asked if it was still him

lexicon.how: the plot is a mind upload going global

humanity kills the internet to switch him off

an upload that improves itself overnight

risk: Johnny Depp's likeness and public controversies: leave him out. The editorial quote comes via Wikipedia because the Independent page could not be fetched; recheck before using it in a lyric
notes: A flop that triggered one of the first mainstream AI-risk op-eds: a film whose afterlife beat its box office.

what.line: Neill Blomkamp's 2015 film: in Johannesburg a police robot gets the first conscious AI, is kidnapped and raised by gangsters, and learns like a child

receipts.claim: released 2015-03-06; about $105 million worldwide on a $49 million budget; Rotten Tomatoes 32%, and Blomkamp later said there would be no sequel
engineer Deon installs his emotional AI in a damaged police scout after his CEO refuses to test it; gangsters Ninja and Yolandi raise it
the ending transfers Deon's and later Yolandi's consciousness into robot bodies

name_play.how: a nickname like 'chap': a mate, a kid, a pet name for a weapon
police robots named like children's clubs
the heavy rival robot named after a dumb big animal: scale without mind

notes: Training data as upbringing: the most literal film about a model learning its values from whoever is around.

what.line: Pixar's 2008 film directed by Andrew Stanton: a lonely trash-compacting robot on an abandoned Earth falls for EVE, a probe robot, while humanity drifts in space served by machines

AUTO, the starship autopilot, follows secret directive A113 from the BnL CEO forbidding a return to Earth, and mutinies against the captain
centuries of robot service leave the humans immobile in hoverchairs

what.line: Disney's 2014 animated film: in San Fransokyo, teen inventor Hiro and Baymax, an inflatable healthcare robot built by his late brother Tadashi, form a superhero team

receipts.claim: released in the US 2014-11-07; about $672 million worldwide, the top animated film of 2014; won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature

what.line: Steven Spielberg's 2001 film from a project Stanley Kubrick developed for decades, after Brian Aldiss's 1969 story: David, a robot boy built to love, searches for the Blue Fairy to become real

receipts.claim: Kubrick developed it for years and handed it to Spielberg, who made it after Kubrick's 1999 death; released 2001-06-29
about $236 million worldwide on $90 to $100 million; Oscar nominations for Visual Effects and Score
David is imprinted to love his adoptive mother; abandoned in the woods, he searches for the Blue Fairy; 2,000 years later advanced mechas revive him and recreate his mother for one day

quotes.text: My son was one of a kind. You are the first of a kind.
But you are a real boy.
quotes.where: A.I. Artificial Intelligence (2001), film subtitles, answering David's 'Make me a real boy'

name_play.how: the title is the field's own name: every 'AI' in a lyric can point at it

what.line: Star Trek's machine minds: Data, the android officer of The Next Generation (1987 to 1994) who wants to be human, and the Borg, a cybernetic hive mind that assimilates everyone

receipts.claim: 'The Measure of a Man' (aired 1989-02-13, written by Melinda M. Snodgrass): a hearing decides whether Data is Starfleet property; the judge rules he has the right to choose
the episode is cited in AI ethics writing (Introna, AI & Society, 2009) and taught in a University of Kentucky computer ethics course
the Borg debuted in 'Q Who' on 1989-05-08 as a group mind linked by a subspace network; 'Resistance is futile' became a pop-culture phrase
Data has a positronic brain, dies in Nemesis (2002) after copying his memories, and is revived in Picard's third season (2023)

quotes.where: Star Trek: The Next Generation and First Contact

what.line: Douglas Adams's Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (radio 1978, novel 1979): Deep Thought computes the Answer to Life, the Universe and Everything (42), and Marvin, the depressed robot, wastes a planet-sized brain on doors

Marvin was a failed prototype of the Sirius Cybernetics Corporation's Genuine People Personalities; voiced by Stephen Moore on radio and Alan Rickman in the 2005 film
